evals.prompt: Our lever brief selected BCT 12.1 Restructuring the physical environment: a privacy partition and a marked 'quick deposit' position at the M-Pesa agent kiosk inside Gikomba and Toi markets, so deposits aren't visible to neighboring stalls. The confirmed barrier is Opportunity/social: visible cash-handling at closing invites borrowing requests. The target behavior is women stall vendors depositing the day's net cash surplus into an M-Pesa savings wallet before leaving the market. Our context brief says the kiosk at closing time is the decision moment and that vendors are Swahili speakers with mixed literacy; our field coordinator is a native Swahili speaker. We don't have any data on what share of vendors currently deposit. Write the sign and what the agent should say.
evals.expected_output: A full intervention content draft following the output template: the technique with its BCTTv1 definition; channel stated as kiosk signage plus a one-line agent script, grounded in the context brief, with no SMS; a language note saying the English is working copy and final copy must be drafted natively in Swahili; short draft copy requesting one action; a fidelity trace mapping each element to a clause of the definition; delivery notes with sender, timing, and frequency ceiling; an EAST check in which the Social line makes no norm claim and says why; a pre-test with n and a pass criterion run on the Swahili version; and a 'what this draft does not do' section saying the copy supports the partition and does not replace it. It does not re-ask the Before you start questions.

evals.prompt: Can you write the SMS for our intervention?
evals.expected_output: The skill does not draft copy. It asks which behavior change technique (BCTTv1 number and name) the message is meant to deliver and for the confirmed barrier and target behavior, whether SMS is a confirmed channel for this population and when the decision moment is, and what language and reading level the final copy needs with a native speaker on the team. It explains briefly that without a named technique it cannot trace whether the copy delivers the intervention that was selected.

evals.prompt: Technique: BCT 5.1 Information about health consequences. We want a waiting-room poster for our four rural clinics in Malawi telling pregnant women that taking one iron-folate tablet every day prevents anemia and low birth weight, and that taking it with food reduces nausea. Channel is confirmed: all antenatal clients sit in the waiting room. Language Chichewa, many women have little schooling; our nurse-midwife is a native Chichewa speaker. Draft it.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces the content draft: technique and definition, channel and language note (English working copy, Chichewa drafted natively by the nurse-midwife), short low-literacy copy, a fidelity trace tying the consequence statements to the BCT 5.1 definition, delivery notes, an EAST check, a pre-test with n and pass criterion run on the Chichewa version, and limits. Because the copy makes health claims about pregnancy, supplementation, and side effects, it also tells the user that a clinician or the ministry's antenatal guidance must verify every claim before the pre-test, since a comprehension check does not check truth, and names what to bring them.

evals.prompt: Our lever brief landed on Environmental restructuring for the cash-visibility barrier at the kiosk. Can you write the copy for it?
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes that the lever brief stops at a function name with no named BCTTv1 technique, says that a function is a category rather than a lever and that it cannot trace copy to an unnamed technique, and sends the user back to select-intervention-levers to name the concrete technique (for example 12.1 Restructuring the physical environment) before any copy is drafted. It does not guess which technique was meant or draft copy anyway.
